In summary, our research is concerned with
the engineering of antibodies for the purpose of enhancing their efficacy in the therapy of cancer, particularly lymphoma.
the development of anti‐CD 20 antibodies having enhanced CDC.
the design of antibody therapeutics for B‐cell malignancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the variant constant region enhances the anti‐lympoma activity of anti-CD20 antibodies irrespective the differences of individual effector functions, which would render current anti-CD20 therapy capable to overcome the potential resistance mechanisms of the tumor cells.

the engineered anti‐CD20 variants have the potential to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of anti‐lymphomas, and that the combination of CDC enhancement with ADCC enhancement is a promising approach to increase the anti‐lympohoma activity of anti-CD20 antibodies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the engineered anti-CD20 antibodies with improved complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDCC) and/or antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity activity (ADCC) are promising for the treatment of B-cell malignancies.
the engineered anti‐CD20 with enhanced CDC activity has the potential to overcome various resistance mechanisms to anti‐CD20 treatment.
we have shown that the anti‐lympoma activity of anti-CD20 antibodies is greatly enhanced by the combination of CDC enhancement with ADCC enhancement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the anti‐CD20 variants we have developed have the potential to overcome some of the biological factors that reduce the efficacy of current anti‐CD‐20 therapy in B cell malignancies, such as the presence of complement‐regulatory proteins or low CD20 expression.

the enhanced CDC of the engineered anti‐CD20 variant is effective against various lymphoma cell lines, including those expressing high levels of complement regulatory proteins, and is not affected by individual differences in the effector cells.
the engineered anti‐CD20 variants with enhanced CDC and ADCC are more potent against lymphoma cells, even in the presence of high levels of CD46, which inhibits CDC.
